name: Statue of Zeus at Olympia
description: Colossal 12.4-meter chryselephantine statue of the king of Greek gods, an Ancient World Wonder.
history: Commissioned by the Eleans for the sanctuary at Olympia, the statue was sculpted by Phidias. Zeus sat upon an elaborate cedarwood throne ornamented with ebony, ivory, gold, and precious gemstones, holding Nike (goddess of victory) in his right hand.
construction: Framed with wood and paneled with sculpted ivory plates for flesh and beaten sheets of solid gold for drapery (chryselephantine technique).
architecture: The statue occupied the entire width of the cella aisle in the Temple of Zeus, appearing so grand that ancient writers remarked if Zeus stood up, he would unroof the temple.
significance: The crowning achievement of ancient Greek classical sculpture and an essential pilgrimage destination during the Ancient Olympic Games.
currentStatus: Destroyed in the 5th century CE by fire (either at Olympia in 426 CE or during the Palace of Lausus fire in Constantinople in 475 CE).
wonderReplacedBy: Replaced in modern global canon by the New 7 Wonders campaign
wonderHistoricalContext: Admired across the Greco-Roman world for eight centuries. After the abolition of the Olympic Games by Christian Emperor Theodosius I, the statue was relocated to Constantinople, where it perished in a palace conflagration in 475 CE.
